Beequation is a mental maths puzzle game: Beequation is a mental maths puzzle game made by Trett Labs Limited in the UK. Each puzzle is a small honeycomb of numbers, and exactly one of them is made from two others: by adding them, or in multiplication-table puzzles, by multiplying them. You find that number and tap it. Puzzles start with sums to 10 for five-year-olds and go up to four-digit numbers, negatives, fractions, decimals, the three-number Trio and the Big Hive for adults.
There are two apps: <b>Beequation Kids</: There are two apps: Beequation Kids for ages 5 to 12, and Beequation Pro for teens and adults, with a new Daily Pro puzzle every day. Both are free to try, have no ads and collect no personal data. Learn how to play or play free in your browser.

How to play Beequation, the mental maths: How to play Beequation, the mental maths puzzle: find the number two others add up or multiply to. Rules, examples and tips.
Every Beequation puzzle is a small honey: Every Beequation puzzle is a small honeycomb of numbers. Exactly one of the numbers is made from two of the others. Find it and tap it.
In most puzzles, the number you're looki: In most puzzles, the number you're looking for is the sum of two others. In this honeycomb, 7 + 5 = 12, so 12 is the one to tap.
Example honeycomb: 7, 3, 12, 5 and 11. T: Example honeycomb: 7, 3, 12, 5 and 11. The answer is 12, because 7 plus 5 is 12.
In times-table puzzles (Times Garden in: In multiplication-table puzzles (Times Garden in Beequation Kids, Times in Beequation Pro), the number is the product of two others. Here, 4 × 6 = 24.
Example honeycomb: 4, 9, 24, 6 and 15. T: Example honeycomb: 4, 9, 24, 6 and 15. The answer is 24, because 4 times 6 is 24.
<b>Start with the big numbers.</b> In an: Start with the big numbers. In an adding puzzle the answer is usually one of the larger numbers, because it's made by adding two others.
<b>Use odd and even.</b> An odd total ne: Use odd and even. An odd total needs one odd and one even number. Two odd numbers, or two even numbers, always make an even total.
<b>Look at the last digit.</b> If the ca: Look at the last digit. If the candidate ends in 2, look for two numbers whose last digits add to 2 or 12, such as 7 and 5.
<b>For times tables, think factors.</b>: For multiplication tables, think factors. Ask which numbers divide the candidate exactly. 24 could be 4 × 6, 3 × 8 or 2 × 12.
<b>Rule numbers out.</b> The smallest nu: Rule numbers out. The smallest number can almost never be a sum of two others, so you can usually skip it.
The Big Hive is a puzzle made of puzzles: The Big Hive is a puzzle made of puzzles. You solve four small combs, and their four answers become a final comb that you solve last.
<b>Beequation Kids</b> (ages 5 to 12) ha: Beequation Kids (ages 5 to 12) has six worlds and 35 levels: Adding Meadow, Times Garden, Fraction Forest, Tens Town (tens and hundreds), Decimal Dunes (tenths and hundredths) and Big Hive. Indie the bee gives a hint when your child is stuck, and stars count hints and slips gently, with no clock.
<b>Beequation Pro</b> (teens and adults): Beequation Pro (teens and adults) has 64 levels from Egg to Hive Mind across adding, times, negatives, fractions, decimals and mixed puzzles, plus Trio, where one number is the sum of three others, a new Daily Pro puzzle every day, and a 60-second blitz. Hard mode gives you one tap per puzzle.
